faq.a: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957. It was a shiny metal ball about 58 centimetres across that sent radio beeps for about three weeks.

faq.q: Who was the first animal in orbit?
faq.a: Laika, a stray dog from Moscow, orbited Earth aboard Sputnik 2 in November 1957. Sadly she died during the flight, as there was no way to bring her back.

faq.q: Who was the first person in space?
faq.a: Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union, on 12 April 1961. His spacecraft, Vostok 1, circled Earth once in 108 minutes.

faq.q: Who walked on the Moon first?
faq.a: Neil Armstrong, followed by Buzz Aldrin, on 20 July 1969 during the US Apollo 11 mission, while Michael Collins orbited above. Twelve people walked on the Moon between 1969 and 1972.
asks: When did people land on the Moon?

faq.q: Why was the Apollo-Soyuz mission important?
faq.a: In July 1975 an American Apollo and a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft docked in orbit, and the crews shook hands. It showed the rivals could cooperate, and led to later partnerships like the International Space Station.
asks: How did the space race end?

facts: Yuri Gagarin's flight on 12 April 1961 lasted 108 minutes.
Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon between 1969 and 1972.

quiz.say: Who was the first human in space?
quiz.show: The first human in space was…
quiz.why: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth on 12 April 1961.

wrong.1: Neil Armstrong was the first to walk on the Moon, in 1969.
wrong.2: Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space, in 1963.

quiz.say: Which country launched the first satellite?
quiz.show: The first satellite was launched by…
quiz.why: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in 1957.

wrong.1: The USA's first satellite, Explorer 1, followed in 1958.
wrong.2: Japan's first satellite was launched in 1970.
